titulo: A preeclampsia prediction model incorporating methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase, vitamin D receptor, and uterine artery pulsatility index.
autores_exibicao: Xu M, Yang G, Zhong X, Jin Z, Tang M, Xiao Y, Guo Y
resumo: OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the predictive value of methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) rs1801133 and vitamin D receptor (VDR) FokI rs2228570 polymorphisms combined with uterine artery pulsatility index (PI) for preeclampsia (PE), and explored mediating pathways underlying genetic risk. METHODS: A two-phase prospective study was conducted. Phase I (n = 73) screened PE-related single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) via targeted sequencing; Phase II (n = 195) validated the candidates and collected clinical and ultrasound metrics. Independent predictors were identified by multivariate logistic regression to build a nomogram, and the nomogram was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration, and decision curve analyses. Mediation analysis was performed to quantify the contribution of serum biomarkers. RESULTS: The T allele of MTHFR rs1801133 showed a marginal association with PE risk under dominant model (OR = 1.82, 95% CI: 0.96-3.44, P = 0.067), while VDR rs2228570 was not significantly associated (OR = 1.74, 95% CI: 0.89-3.39, P = 0.104). Pre-pregnancy body mass index (BMI) ≥25 kg/m² (OR = 2.75, 95% CI: 1.45-5.21, P = 0.002) and elevated uterine artery PI (OR = 4.75, 95% CI: 1.38-16.41, P = 0.014) were independent risk factors. The nomogram achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.711 (95% CI: 0.640-0.783), with sensitivity of 75.53% and specificity of 59.41%. Asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA) and 8-iso-PGF2α mediated 77.5% and 26.0% of the effect of MTHFR on PE risk, respectively. CONCLUSION: Pre-pregnancy BMI and uterine artery PI are independent predictors of PE. The integrated model offers moderate predictive value. ADMA-mediated endothelial dysfunction may be involved in MTHFR-related PE risk.

titulo: Association of LATE-NC With Neuropathologic Lesions and Cognitive Abilities: A Population-Based Autopsy Study.
autores_exibicao: Matos Silva C, Justo AFO, Ribeiro Paes V, Grinberg LT, Pasqualucci CA, Ferriolli E, Nitrini R, Nelson PT et al. (10 autores)
resumo: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy neuropathologic change (LATE-NC) is a common finding in aging brains. However, most previous studies were limited to ethnoracially homogeneous cohorts from high-income countries. The objective of this study was to investigate the associations between LATE-NC, cognitive performance, and coexisting neuropathologic lesions in a large, ethnoracially and socioeconomically diverse sample from Brazil. METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed data from the Biobank for Aging Studies, a Brazilian population-based autopsy study based at the University of São Paulo. The study included a consecutive series of autopsies performed between 2004 and 2024. Inclusion criteria required participants to be at least 18 years old with a knowledgeable informant. LATE-NC, Alzheimer disease neuropathologic change (ADNC), Lewy body pathology (LBP), lacunar infarcts, small vessel disease, cerebral amyloid angiopathy, and hippocampal sclerosis were assessed following international criteria. Cognitive abilities were evaluated with the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDR-SOB). Logistic and linear regression models were applied to examine associations of LATE-NC with comorbid neuropathologies and cognitive outcomes, with adjustments for sociodemographic, clinical, and neuropathologic covariates. RESULTS: The sample comprised 1,860 participants (mean age = 72.6 ± 14.2 years; 49.1% female; 62.2% White; 35.4% Black). LATE-NC was present in 7.4% of participants (stage 1: 3.0%; stage 2: 4.0%; stage 3: 0.4%). After adjustment for sociodemographic, clinical, and other neuropathologic covariates, LATE-NC (stages 2-3) was associated with hippocampal sclerosis (OR = 14.95; 95% CI 7.42-30.27; p < 0.001), advanced Braak NFT stages (OR = 2.23; 95% CI 1.32-3.83; p = 0.003), and LBP (OR = 1.89; 95% CI 1.02-3.37; p = 0.036). Factoring in other pathologies, LATE-NC was associated with the CDR-SOB score (β = 4.06; 95% CI 2.95-5.18; p < 0.001), demonstrating a consistent association with cognition, similar to the one observed for moderate/severe ADNC (β = 3.78; 95% CI 3.14-4.42; p < 0.001) in the same sample. DISCUSSION: LATE-NC was prevalent and associated with cognitive impairment in this ethnoracially and socioeconomically diverse sample. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and some estimates had wide confidence intervals due to the small number of advanced-stage cases.

titulo: Development and internal validation of a machine learning model for predicting second primary malignancy risk in hodgkin lymphoma survivors: a population-based competing risk analysis.
autores_exibicao: Li S, Xiong M, Gan Z, Lu H, Zhao Y, Huang H, Yi T
resumo: BACKGROUND: Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) survivors face an elevated long-term risk of developing second primary malignancies (SPMs), yet accurate prediction tools remain scarce. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a machine learning-based prediction model for SPM risk in HL survivors using a competing risk framework. METHODS: We analysed 57,429 patients diagnosed with HL between 2006 and 2020 from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 40,201, 70%) and internal validation (n = 17,228, 30%) cohorts. A random survival forest (RSF) model was developed to predict SPM occurrence, with death without SPM treated as a competing event. Model performance was compared against the traditional Fine-Grey subdistribution hazard regression. Discrimination was assessed using time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and calibration was evaluated through calibration plots. Clinical utility was determined via decision curve analysis (DCA). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was employed to interpret the model. RESULTS: During follow-up, 4,954 patients (8.6%) developed SPMs, while 9,750 (17.0%) died without SPM. The RSF model demonstrated superior discriminative ability compared to Fine-Grey regression across all time points: AUC at 3 years (0.721 vs. 0.549), 5 years (0.761 vs. 0.555), and 10 years (0.804 vs. 0.553). Calibration plots indicated good agreement between predicted and observed risks. DCA confirmed the RSF model provided greater net clinical benefit across a wide range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis identified age as the most influential predictor, followed by disease stage, radiotherapy status, race, sex, and chemotherapy. CONCLUSIONS: The RSF-based machine learning model accurately predicts SPM risk in HL survivors within a competing risk framework, substantially outperforming traditional regression approaches. This interpretable prediction tool may facilitate personalised surveillance strategies and risk-adapted follow-up for HL survivors.

titulo: Development and validation of machine learning prognostic models for overall survival in non-surgical prostate cancer patients with bone metastases.
autores_exibicao: Yang Q, Wang B, Yang Y, Li S, Li Y, Du Q, Bao E
periodico: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
resumo: OBJECTIVE: To construct and interpret a machine learning model for predicting overall survival in nonsurgical prostate cancer with bone metastases (PCBM). METHODS: Data from 3,378 SEER database patients were utilized to develop machine learning survival models, with the best-performing model visually interpreted using SHAP. RESULTS: The Extra Survival Trees (EST) model performed best (validation AUC = 0.694, C-index = 0.643). SHAP analysis identified the Gleason score as the most critical survival factor, significantly outweighing clinical T stage. Visceral metastasis and advanced age also markedly increased mortality risk. CONCLUSION: The EST model effectively assesses OS in nonsurgical PCBM. The Gleason score holds greater prognostic value than local anatomical staging in this cohort, suggesting clinicians should prioritize early, aggressive combination treatments for high-Gleason, high-burden patients.

titulo: Early prediction of preeclampsia among the advanced-age pregnant women: A retrospective multicenter study.
autores_exibicao: He A, Li X, Yip KC, Wu X, He S, Peng L, Li L, Kong J et al. (12 autores)
periodico: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)
resumo: BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia (PE) remains a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity. Women of advanced maternal age (AMA, ≥ 35 years) constitute a rapidly expanding high-risk subpopulation in China. Existing first-trimester prediction models were derived in general obstetric populations and often rely on specialized biophysical or proprietary biomarker assays, with limited validation in AMA women. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study enrolled 2,582 AMA pregnant women from three tertiary centers in southern China, partitioned into a training cohort (n = 1,327), an internal validation cohort (n = 569), and two external validation cohorts (n = 399 and 287). Predictors were selected using LASSO and multivariable logistic regression and assembled into a nomogram. Performance was evaluated by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, Brier scores, decision curve analysis, and clinical impact curves. RESULTS: Seven independent predictors were retained: pre-pregnancy BMI, parity, mode of conception, uric acid, white blood cell count, red blood cell count, and hemoglobin. The nomogram achieved AUCs of 0.819, 0.795, 0.787, and 0.756 across the four cohorts, with close calibration and favorable net benefit. Performance was preserved when women with chronic hypertension were included and across early-onset and late-onset PE subgroups. Notably, maternal age itself was not discriminative within the AMA stratum (P = 0.626). CONCLUSIONS: This nomogram relying exclusively on routine clinical and laboratory parameters provides an accessible tool for individualized early-pregnancy PE risk assessment and risk-stratified antenatal management in AMA women.

titulo: Explainable Machine Learning for Perioperative Risk Stratification of Radiographic Adjacent Segment Degeneration After Short-Segment Lumbar Fusion.
autores_exibicao: Yao R, Wang D, Cui P, Fan Z, Wang Q, Chen X, Lu J, Lu S
resumo: STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. OBJECTIVES: To develop and externally validate an explainable machine-learning framework for perioperative risk stratification of radiographic adjacent segment degeneration (ASDeg) after short-segment lumbar fusion. SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Radiographic ASDeg is frequently observed after lumbar fusion and may represent an early structural phenotype preceding symptomatic adjacent segment disease (ASDis) in some patients. However, existing risk assessment approaches are limited by heterogeneous risk factors, insufficient model interpretability, and limited external validation. Machine-learning methods may improve perioperative risk stratification by integrating clinical, radiographic, surgical, and functional variables. METHODS: Clinical data were retrospectively collected from two hospitals. The internal cohort included 570 patients who underwent posterior short-segment lumbar fusion for lumbar degenerative disease, and an independent cohort of 150 patients from another institution was used for external validation. The internal cohort was randomly divided into training and internal test sets at a 7:3 ratio using stratified sampling according to ASDeg status. Feature selection was performed exclusively in the training set using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression (LASSO), random forest-recursive feature elimination (RE-RFE), and Boruta. Five algorithms were developed and compared: logistic regression, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and multilayer perceptron (MLP). Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, precision-recall (P-R) analysis, and decision-curve analysis (DCA). Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation. RESULTS: Radiographic ASDeg occurred in 212 of 570 patients in the internal cohort. Five perioperative variables were retained for model construction: preoperative intervertebral space height (ISH), postoperative pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis (PI-LL) mismatch, frailty, Coflex implantation, and preoperative Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC)-defined lower-extremity dysfunction. Among the candidate algorithms, the RF model showed the highest discriminative performance, with an AUROC of 0.782 in the internal test set and 0.749 in the external validation cohort. SHAP analysis identified preoperative ISH as the strongest contributor to model output. CONCLUSIONS: This externally validated RF-based model provides a structured and interpretable framework for postoperative radiographic ASDeg risk stratification after short-segment lumbar fusion. By integrating clinically accessible perioperative variables, the model may support individualized imaging follow-up and provide a preliminary basis for future studies using symptomatic adjacent segment disease or revision surgery as clinically oriented endpoints.

titulo: Individualized Treatment Effect Inference of Head and Neck Cancer with Multimodal Data.
autores_exibicao: Wei Y, Li Z, Woo J, Ouyang J, El Fakhri G, Liu X
periodico: APSIPA Transactions on Signal and Information Processing
resumo: Estimating individualized treatment effects (ITE) is critical for personalized medicine, yet it remains a challenge due to retrospective observational data, which suffer from selection bias in clinical practice, and the complexity of multimodal data used for patient status depiction. In this work, we develop an end-to-end deep learning (DL) framework that incorporates multimodal patient data and multiple treatments for accurate ITE inference in a retrospective head and neck cancer (HNC) study. A possible solution is concatenating the factors and adapt adversarial training, which has shown great promise on tabular data, to disentangle patient characteristics from patient status features to mitigate treatment selection bias. However, this approach suffers from instability when applied to complex multimodal patient data and multiple treatment options. For flexible and efficient, treatment-conditioned information fusion, we propose a bi-stage adaptive instance normalization (Bi-AdaIN) to inject relevant factors into corresponding layers, an approach that is also robust to missing values. Furthermore, we propose to disentangle status features from the multi-treatment variable using mutual information (MI) regularization, enabling more accurate predictions of patient-specific outcomes for both factual and counterfactual data. We evaluated our model on the RADCURE dataset, comprising 3,346 HNC cases with CT scans and multiple clinical variables who received radiotherapy or additional chemotherapy and EGFRI. The Bias-Adjusted Treatment Effect (BATE) is substantially reduced compared to the conventional direct ITE method (which does not consider treatment bias) and to adversarial training, indicating a more robust estimation of causal effects. This work is one of the first DL-based studies to address ITE estimation using multimodal medical imaging, offering a promising approach to counterfactual reasoning in clinical oncology for decision support.

titulo: Machine learning combined with fMRI identifies dynamic brain network alterations in post-stroke depression: A dual-center cross-sectional study.
autores_exibicao: Hu L, Guo Z, Zhao M, Wang Y, Sun F, Tan W, Tian F
resumo: OBJECTIVE: Post-stroke depression (PSD) is under-recognized and associated with poorer rehabilitation outcomes and quality of life. We characterized PSD-related alterations in large-scale brain network dynamics and evaluated their cross-center classification performance. METHODS: This dual-center cross-sectional study included 300 patients with post-stroke motor impairment: 100 with and 100 without PSD in the development cohort, and 50 per group in the external validation cohort. Resting-state functional MRI, sliding-window dynamic functional connectivity, and clustering across K = 2-8 state resolutions were combined with nested cross-validation, nine machine-learning classifiers, and SHAP interpretation. Sensitivity analysis excluded users of antidepressants, anxiolytics, or sedative-hypnotics. RESULTS: The five-state solution provided the best balance of discrimination and interpretability. The support vector machine achieved internally cross-validated and external validation AUCs of 0.838 and 0.784, respectively. Higher proportion and longer dwell time of a globally integrated state, lower proportion and dwell time of a stable modular state, and higher self-transition probability of a low-integration state shifted classification toward PSD. After medication users were excluded, the artificial neural network under the five-state solution achieved internally cross-validated and external validation AUCs of 0.798 and 0.793, respectively; a higher proportion of the globally integrated state also remained among the most informative features. CONCLUSIONS: PSD was associated with altered temporal organization and reduced stability of large-scale functional networks. Dynamic state features may serve as interpretable candidate imaging markers for PSD classification, but longitudinal multicenter validation is required before clinical application.

titulo: Predicting early psychiatric readmission among people with major depressive disorder: A machine learning analysis from the prospective multicentre DEEP READ study.
autores_exibicao: Bartoli F, Luciano M, Crocamo C, Bassetti C, Cavaleri D, Aguglia A, Atti AR, Berardelli I et al. (30 autores)
resumo: BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with high relapse rates, with around 20% of inpatients experiencing readmission within 90 days after discharge. Routinely collected clinical information may help identify individuals at higher risk of readmission. Machine learning (ML) models could complement more traditional statistical approaches by exploring complex relationships among multiple vulnerability factors. METHODS: The DEEP READ study is a prospective, multicentre cohort study conducted across 13 Italian provinces, enrolling adults aged 18-65 years with a DSM-5-TR MDD diagnosis between January 2024 and December 2025. The primary outcome was unplanned psychiatric readmission within 90 days. Sociodemographic and clinical features (including Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores and DSM-5 specifiers), comorbidities, and pharmacological treatment at discharge were recorded. A Random Forest classifier was trained on 22 predictors and internally evaluated using stratified 5-fold cross-validation. RESULTS: The sample included 322 individuals (mean age 43.0 years; 38.5% men), of whom 15.5% (n = 50) were readmitted within 90 days. The model achieved a mean test AUC of 0.74 (range: 0.59-0.87). Suicide attempts, prior hospitalisations, anticonvulsant prescription, cluster B personality disorder, female sex, and anxious distress ranked among the leading predictors. Although exploratory, lithium prescription showed a negative SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) pattern. CONCLUSIONS: A ML model based on routinely collected data showed moderate discrimination for 90-day readmission in MDD. These findings suggest that standard clinical variables may hold predictive value for early readmission. However, external validation, assessment of model calibration, and clinical utility are needed prior to clinical implementation.

titulo: SPISE index and ensemble machine learning refine cardiovascular risk stratification in stage 0-3 CKM syndrome.
autores_exibicao: Wang L, Wang H, Liu T, Zhang N, Zhao L
periodico: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
resumo: BACKGROUND: While the single-point insulin sensitivity estimator (SPISE) shows promise as an insulin resistance biomarker, its association with cardiovascular disease (CVD) in early CKM stages (0-3) remains underexplored. METHODS: We analyzed 6480 participants with CKM stage 0-3 from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. CVD outcomes were assessed relative to SPISE index levels. An ensemble machine learning model was employed to predict CVD risk. RESULTS: 6480 subjects were enrolled, of whom 967 developed CVD. After stratifying participants into SPISE quartiles (Q1-Q4) and adjusting for covariates, higher quartiles were linked to a lower CVD risk. This study developed an LR+GMM (Logistic Regression + Gaussian Mixture Model) ensemble model to predict CVD risk using five strong predictors: SPISE, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-c), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), body mass index (BMI), and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c). The model performed well, achieving an accuracy (ACC) of 0.986 and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.932. CONCLUSIONS: The SPISE index is a significant inverse predictor of CVD risk in individuals with stage 0-3 CKM syndrome. The LR+GMM ensemble model, incorporating the SPISE index and four clinical metrics, demonstrated outstanding predictive performance.

titulo: Analysis of a recent human parvovirus B19 outbreak using a new genomic surveillance system.
autores_exibicao: Cordsmeier A, Steininger P, Albrecht JC, Korn K, Ensser A
resumo: Human parvovirus B19 is the causative agent of various clinical diseases like erythema infectiosum, transient aplastic crisis, fetal hydrops, reactive arthritis, and rarely potentially fatal organ diseases. The worldwide seroprevalence of parvovirus B19 has been assessed to be about 40-60%. It has been shown that parvoviruses can also infect new host species, adapt, and co-evolve. A comprehensive genomic surveillance is essential to gain a better insight in the adaptation, evolution, and also epidemics of parvoviruses. In the scope of the large parvovirus B19 epidemic 2023/24 following the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, we developed a rapid and convenient system to analyze parvovirus B19 genomes directly from patient samples by next-generation sequencing. We utilized this system to study the part of the unusual outbreak in Southern Germany (Central Franconia), comprising the counties Nuremberg, Fuerth, and Erlangen. This detected a certain genetic diversity within the analyzed samples and identified shared mutations in comparison to reference sequences. Here, two phylogenetically distinct groups were observed, compatible with the co-circulation of at least two B19V lineages in the region and a putative new genotype of human parvovirus B19, possibly induced by immunosuppression was identified. We established a new, quick, and convenient surveillance system for human parvovirus B19 that enables the analysis of outbreaks and monitoring of viral genetic changes.

titulo: Carbapenemase-encoding genes in surface waters of three cities in Côte d'Ivoire: towards wastewater-based epidemiology and risk assessment.
autores_exibicao: Aboubakar D, Hammer-Dedet F, Bernaud N, Bouazizi I, Masnou A, Toubiana M, Séguis L, Perrin JL et al. (13 autores)
resumo: BACKGROUND: The World Health Organization has emphasised the importance of water sanitation in the environmental spread and transmission of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Global burden projections indicate that Africa will be severely affected by AMR. This pilot survey examines the resistance to carbapenems, an alarming resistance, in aquatic environments in three cities in Côte d'Ivoire. METHODS: 40 water samples were studied, 29 from urban drain ditches and 11 from peri-urban rivers. Carbapenemase-Encoding Genes (CEG) (bla NDM, bla KPC, bla OXA-48, bla VIM, bla IMP), AMR genes and integrase genes, were investigated by end-point and chip real-time PCR. Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (CPE) were also screened. RESULTS: CEGs were detected in 62% of ditches. The bla OXA-48 gene was the most widespread, followed by the bla NDM and the bla KPC genes, detected in 48%, 38% and 24% of samples, respectively. CPE were also isolated. The presence of CEGs appeared to be independent of the presence of AMR genes and integrase genes. In the Djibi watershed, the detection rate of CEG was linked to the level of urbanisation: 1 or 2 CEGs were detected in 100% of samples from urbanised sites, while 40% were positive only for bla OXA-48 in natural areas further away from Abidjan. CONCLUSIONS: Detection of CEG and CPE in aquatic environments in Côte d'Ivoire demonstrates the role of environment in AMR emergence in an active human/environment cycle. Monitoring CEGs in aquatic environments would provide a means of assessing AMR in human populations. This should serve as a warning against the silent faecal/oral transmission of CPEs/CEGs in middle-income countries.

titulo: Delayed and nonlinear associations and predictive causal signals between climate factors, air pollutants, and influenza epidemics in 48 countries.
autores_exibicao: Wang D, Li N, Li X, Wu X, Zhao L, Dong G, Yin J
resumo: BACKGROUND: Influenza remains a recurring threat to global health with pandemic potential, yet the predictive causal associations of climate factors and air pollutants on its transmission remain not fully quantified. Thus, this study aimed to quantify the nonlinear and delayed effects of these factors, as well as their predictive causal signals for global influenza epidemics. METHODS: This study was a longitudinal time-series analysis conducted across 48 countries from 2022 to 2024. Weekly influenza positivity rates were derived from the FluNet database and integrated with climate variables and air pollutants. Spatiotemporal Bayesian models were constructed separately for the Northern and Southern Hemispheres to quantify the nonlinear and lagged effects of climate variables and air pollutants while accounting for socioeconomic conditions. Predictive causal relationships were further assessed using convergent cross mapping (CCM) to identify potential environmental drivers for influenza transmission. RESULTS: In Northern Hemisphere countries, the highest odds ratio (OR) for influenza was 1.74 (95% CI: 1.34-2.26) at weekly cumulative SO2 concentrations of 3100 μg/m3 with a 1.6-week lag, and 2.36 (95% CI: 1.53-3.64) at a temperature of -27 °C with a 2.2-week lag. In Southern Hemisphere countries, the highest OR was 1.72 (95% CI: 0.65-4.58) at weekly cumulative organic carbon (OC) concentrations of 5800 μg/m3 with a 3.2-week lag, and 1.31 (95% CI: 1.00-1.71) corresponding to a temperature of 14 °C with a lag of 2 weeks. CCM analysis identified PM2.5 in dust and wind speed as the dominant drivers among air pollutants and climate factors, respectively. PM2.5 in dust influenced influenza in 19 countries, while wind speed did so in 15 countries across the study area. CONCLUSIONS: Climate variables and air pollutants exhibited nonlinear and lagged effects on influenza transmission, with key air pollutants varying across hemispheres. Predictive causal signals of selected climate variables were further modulated by specific socioeconomic conditions. These findings highlight the importance of integrating environmental and socioeconomic conditions, providing practical guidance for implementing targeted influenza control strategies.

titulo: Descriptive epidemiology of measles in the southern region of Afghanistan, 2024-2025: a secondary analysis from regional case-based surveillance data.
autores_exibicao: Naeemi S, Rahimi M, Niazi NA, Sakhi R
resumo: OBJECTIVES: After a three-fold increase in measles outbreaks in Afghanistan during 2024, this study aimed to assess the descriptive epidemiology of measles in the southern region. METHODS: This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted on case-based measles surveillance data retrieved from the District Health Information System 2 for the period from January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2025. Demographic, clinical, and immunization status data were summarized descriptively and surveillance system performance was assessed using World Health Organization indicators. RESULTS: Of 4379 suspected measles cases, 3346 (76.4%) were laboratory-confirmed and 52.7% were males. The median age was 24 months (interquartile range 12-60), and four-fifths were children aged under 5 years. A total of 66.5% of cases were from Kandahar; overall, 80.9% of all cases and 80.2% of confirmed cases did not have a measles-containing vaccine record. Helmand had the highest proportion of unvaccinated cases at 97.7%. The overall discarded rate was 10.55 per 100,000 population; the adequate time for investigation, specimen adequacy, laboratory receipt of specimen, and communication of results with public health authorities were 98.3%, 99.1%, 77.7%, and 82.8%, respectively. CONCLUSION: Measles transmission in southern Afghanistan during 2024-2025 was predominantly recorded along with a large unvaccinated population for measles-containing vaccine, concentrated in children aged under 5 years, with highlighted provincial disparities in immunization and surveillance timeliness. Geographically differentiated responses prioritizing outreach vaccination and strengthening specimen transport in the lowest-performing provinces are urgently required.

titulo: Epidemiological and virological characteristics of influenza in Zhejiang Province, China: A 15-year surveillance study.
autores_exibicao: Jin J, Yu Z, Zhu Y, Cao Y, Zhang H, Wang X, Sun J
resumo: Understanding the complex epidemiological and virological characteristics of influenza is critical for optimizing seasonal influenza control and prevention programs; to this end, we analyzed the influenza and influenza-like illness (ILI) cases reported in Zhejiang Province from 2010 to 2025. Annual average percentage (AAP) approach was used to estimate the influenza seasonal epidemic onset and duration. Generalized additive model (GAM) was used to explore the nonlinear relationship between age and the positive rate of influenza. Spearman correlation analysis was performed to assess the association between weekly ILI% and influenza positivity rate. A total of 5,853,160 influenza cases and 8,732,124 ILI cases were reported. The ILI% ranged from 2.49 to 6.84% (mean: 4.37%), with the lowest level in 2010-2011 and the highest in 2023-2024. The median duration of seasonal influenza epidemics was 4.59 months (IQR: 2.84-5.88). Children aged 5~14 y had the highest influenza positivity rate (41.73%). Influenza virus subtypes/lineages varied significantly by seasons and age groups. A/H3N2 was the predominant pathogen during the summer seasons and the positivity rate of A/H3N2 was much higher than that of other subtypes/lineages among individuals aged ≤60 y. ILI% was positively correlated with influenza positivity during 2010-2025 except in the 2020-2021 surveillance year. This study revealed significant variations in seasonal epidemic period and age-specific distributions across influenza subtypes/lineages, as well as a marked disruption of influenza activity due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

titulo: Genomic epidemiology of CHIKV during the largest outbreak in Mainland China - implication for CHIKV intervention.
autores_exibicao: Yi L, Xiang S, Huang X, Huang J, Chen M, Long H, He Y, Zeng C et al. (13 autores)
resumo: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has caused recurrent epidemics across tropical and subtropical regions globally. In 2025, Guangdong, China, experienced the largest documented CHIKV outbreak in mainland China, with 23,464 reported cases across all 21 prefecture-level cities. We conducted integrated epidemiological, genomic, and phylodynamic analyses to investigate the outbreak's origins, transmission dynamics, and CHIKV lineage evolution. The Guangdong strain belongs to the East/Central/South African (ECSA) genotype, Middle African lineage (ECSA-MAL) - one of several CHIKV lineages co-circulating globally in 2025; a long internal branch separates ECSA-MAL from previously sequenced relatives, indicating substantial surveillance gaps in endemic regions. Phylodynamic analysis using a local molecular clock model estimated that the viral introduction occurred within a narrow window in early April 2025 (95% HPD: March 26-April 12), suggesting a 2.5-month period of cryptic transmission prior to detection. The prolonged silent phase aligns with vector dynamics: the Mosquito Ovitrap Index in the outbreak town of Beijiao, Foshan, stayed low in April (3.0) before surging to 9.0 through July - consistent with suppressed early transmission followed by seasonal amplification. Human migration from the two epidemic epicenters was moderately associated with the spatial distribution of cases (Spearman ρ around 0.5), while mosquito ecology may constrain spatial spread. Phylowave analysis on global circulating strains identified 33 lineage-defining mutations across 14 sublineages, concentrated in NSP3, E1 and E2. Four of these have been experimentally validated as adaptive mutations. This study demonstrates the critical need for enhanced genomic surveillance during pre-peak months and underscores the importance of monitoring adaptive mutations across diverse ecological regions.

titulo: Impact of the two-dose varicella vaccination recommendation program and surveillance optimization on epidemiological trends in a megacity in China.
autores_exibicao: Liu Y, Xu J, Zhang H, Xu J, Zhang Y, Wang Q, Ji H, Zhou C et al. (9 autores)
resumo: To assess the impact of implementing a two-dose varicella vaccine (VarV) immunization recommendation program on the incidence of varicella in Chongqing, China. Monthly reported varicella cases from 2011 to 2023 were extracted from the National Notifiable Diseases Reporting System (NNDRS), alongside the vaccination records from the Chongqing Immunization Planning Information Management System. The interrupted time series analysis (ITS) was employed to study the epidemiological trends of varicella. The average reported annual incidence of varicella in Chongqing was 69.6 per 100,000 population during 2011-2023, with the highest incidence recorded in 2019 (133.9 per 100,000 population) and the lowest in 2011 (21.3 per 100,000 population). Children aged 5-9 y accounted for 34.5% of the total cases. Second-dose coverage of VarV surged from 4.1% in 2018 to 27.5% in 2023 among children aged 4-6 y. The segmented regression model demonstrated that, following the incorporation of varicella into the surveillance system in 2014, there was an upward long-term trend in the reported varicella incidence (β3 = 0.118, P < .01). Following the implementation of the two-dose VarV recommendation strategy in January 2019, a significant long-term decline trend was observed (β5 = -0.209, P < .01). The official inclusion of varicella into the notifiable disease surveillance can improve the detection, reporting, and evaluation of varicella cases in real-world settings. The implementation of a two-dose VarV recommendation strategy, along with increased coverage of the second dose, can effectively reduce the varicella incidence. Maintaining sensitive surveillance and adhering to the two-dose vaccination schedule are crucial for controlling varicella epidemics.

titulo: Nationwide clinical-genomic epidemiology of listeriosis in Taiwan, 2018-2025: disease manifestations in relation to clonal background.
autores_exibicao: Chiou CS, Wang KC, Chang JH, Wei HL, Hong YP, Liao YS, Wang YW, Kuo SC et al. (10 autores)
resumo: Listeriosis is an uncommon but severe foodborne infection, yet nationwide data linking pathogen genomics with clinical manifestations remain limited. We analyzed 1,252 laboratory-confirmed symptomatic listeriosis cases reported through nationwide surveillance in Taiwan during 2018-2025, with whole-genome sequencing of the corresponding clinical Listeria monocytogenes isolate from every case. The average annual incidence was 6.68 cases per 1,000,000 person-years, and 30-day all-cause mortality was 11.4%. Incidence showed an age-dependent sex pattern, with higher incidence among females aged 15-44 years and a shift toward male predominance at older ages. The female excess at ages 15-44 years persisted after exclusion of documented maternal-neonatal cases (male-to-female incidence rate ratio, 0.57; 95% confidence interval, 0.36-0.89). Clonal complex 87 (CC87) was the predominant CC (35.9%), whereas CC1 and CC2 were associated with higher odds of central nervous system (CNS) infection. LIPI-4 occurred predominantly in CC87, and LIPI-4-positive isolates showed lower odds of CNS infection; however, this association could not be separated from clonal background. More broadly, most associations of pathogenicity islands, virulence genes, and their alleles with disease manifestations could not be separated from the underlying clonal backgrounds in which these markers occurred, and none of the estimable associations remained significant after CC adjustment. This nationwide clinical-genomic study characterizes the contemporary burden of listeriosis in Taiwan and highlights clonal background as essential context for interpreting associations between virulence markers and disease manifestations.

titulo: Planning and implementation of a community-wide tuberculosis screening intervention: a case study from Naujaat, Nunavut, Canada.
autores_exibicao: Xie XT, Batac ALR, Wills O, Kulleperuma K, Dhillon A, Palaniappan S, Agyemang EA
resumo: In Nunavut, public health management of tuberculosis (TB) remains a challenge due to social and economic inequities, geographic isolation, TB-related stigma, and distrust in healthcare linked to a history of colonialism. A TB outbreak was declared in Naujaat, Nunavut following an increase in reported cases starting in January 2023. In response to this outbreak, the Naujaat community-wide TB screening (CWS) clinic was held from April 15th to May 29th, 2024, with support from the Nunavut Tunavik Incorporated (NTI) leadership and community engagement teams. This article outlines the steps taken in the coordination and implementation of a large public health intervention in this remote, northern community. Despite significant logistical challenges, the CWS clinic screened 89.2% of the 1000-person target consisting of all previously unscreened individuals residing in the community. As a result, 31 individuals with latent TB infection and <5 active TB cases were diagnosed and offered treatment, representing nearly 4% of those undergoing 2-step testing. Although the screening outcomes suggested that community transmission was low at the time of community-wide screening, it nonetheless exceeded the WHO threshold of 0.5% prevalence for community-wide screening. Lessons learned through the Naujaat CWS can help inform future public health actions towards TB elimination in Nunavut and other circumpolar jurisdictions.

titulo: Resurgence of measles in the United States: Examining the outbreak, vaccine hesitancy, and future directions.
autores_exibicao: Edward M
resumo: The United States is experiencing a resurgence of measles, a highly contagious disease previously declared eliminated in 2000. This article examines the current trends of this resurgence, focusing on the increasing number of cases and outbreaks, the factors contributing to low vaccination rates, and the critical role of vaccine hesitancy. Data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) as of May 15, 2025, are presented, highlighting the significant increase in measles activity and the concentration of cases within outbreaks. The analysis explores the epidemiological characteristics of these outbreaks, including severity and transmission dynamics, and examines the decline in national MMR vaccine coverage. Finally, the article discusses evidence-based strategies to enhance vaccine accessibility, combat misinformation, and improve outbreak response, emphasizing the urgent need for a coordinated public health approach to mitigate future outbreaks and protect vulnerable populations.

titulo: A cross-sectional evaluation of medicine shortages in community pharmacy: implications for patients, pharmacists and clinical service expansion.
autores_exibicao: Aminou Y, Horan N, Dwyer SO, Uileagoid EM, Bennett-Lenane H
periodico: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
resumo: BACKGROUND: Community pharmacists play a pivotal role in managing medicine shortages (MSs) internationally. Ireland presents an interesting case study to assess the impact of MSs in community pharmacy, owing in part to its small market size. OBJECTIVES: Accordingly, this study aimed to explore Irish pharmacists' perceptions of MSs, their causes and impact on staff, and patients. A further aim was to investigate their impact on newly introduced clinical pharmacy services. METHOD: Study design utilised a cross-sectional questionnaire comprising multiple choice, Likert-scale and open text questions, disseminated to community pharmacists. Responses were coded and analysed quantitatively using descriptive and inferential statistics. Open-text responses were analysed using reflective thematic analysis. RESULTS: Data were collected from 270 pharmacists (6.5% response rate). Over 70% (71.1%, n = 192) perceived an increase in MSs over the past year. Commonly reported causes of MSs were manufacturer allocations (69.8%, n = 185) and manufacturing disruptions (66.4%, n = 176). Impacts of MSs on staff included increased administrative duties (94.8%, n = 238) and work-related stress (97.0% (n = 260). Pharmacists reported a median of four hours per week spent addressing MSs (IQR 4.0, n = 236). Almost two thirds believed patient health outcomes had been negatively affected (62.8%, n = 169). Patient impacts included treatment interruptions (82.8%, n = 140) and distress and inconvenience (97.6%, n = 165). Regarding clinical services, almost half of respondents (46.3%, n = 124) indicated prescribing challenges due to MSs. Open text comments revealed recommendations for improved communication and collaboration. CONCLUSION: Proactive collaboration among stakeholders is essential to alleviate pressures in managing MSs, improve patient care and support clinical role expansion.

titulo: Analytical description of adverse events with long-acting injectable cabotegravir and rilpivirine in people living with HIV: a large multicentre prospective observational cohort study (SCOLTA).
autores_exibicao: Cologgi G, Ricci E, Di Biagio A, Ferrara S, Orofino G, Squillace N, Pontali E, Menzaghi B et al. (19 autores)
tipo: Journal Article, Observational Study, Multicenter Study
resumo: INTRODUCTION: Long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine (LA CAB+RPV) is a highly effective, well-tolerated antiretroviral regimen, but real-world adverse event (AE) data remain limited. We characterised the type and frequency of AEs associated with LA CAB+RPV in people with HIV in routine clinical practice. METHODS: This multicentre, prospective, observational study (SCOLTA project, Italy) enrolled people with HIV initiating LA CAB+RPV. Clinical characteristics, AEs and discontinuations were systematically collected. A centre-level survey assessed AE management and prevention practices. RESULTS: In our cohort 598 people with HIV were enrolled across 25 centres. Forty-two participants (7%) experienced overall 51 AEs, of which 37 (88%) led to discontinuation of LA injectable therapy. Injection site reactions (ISRs) were the most frequently reported AEs (29.4%). Central nervous system (CNS)-related AEs accounted for 7.8% of events and resulted in treatment discontinuation in 75% of cases. In multivariable analysis, unknown HIV acquisition mode was independently associated with an increased risk of AEs. Age ≥50 years showed a consistent trend across all models and was the only significant independent predictor in sensitivity analyses restricted to people with HIV with known HIV acquisition mode. Among the 23 centres responding to the survey, 15 (65.2%) reported a reduction in injection-related events following specific training of staff administering LA CAB+RPV. CONCLUSIONS: LA CAB+RPV showed a lower AE rate than pivotal trials, despite more AE-related discontinuations. CNS-related AEs were uncommon, supporting good tolerability, but led to discontinuation when they occurred. Older age was independently associated with increased AE risk.

titulo: Artificial intelligence in pharmacy and pharmaceutical sciences: Research output, trends, and thematic priorities - A descriptive analysis of web of science-indexed publications (2010-2025).
autores_exibicao: Salman B, Mohamed A, Shaikh AJ, Al-Mahrizi A, Al-Shidi R, Al-Farsi S, Hashish N, Al-Kiyumi Z et al. (10 autores)
periodico: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
resumo: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming pharmacy and pharmaceutical sciences (PPS), yet the evolution, research priorities, and global landscape of AI-related research within this field have not been comprehensively characterized. METHODS: A descriptive bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection was conducted for studies published between 2010 and November 9, 2025. Publication trends, document characteristics, journals, publishers, countries, authors, research themes, citation impact, and funding organizations were analyzed using descriptive statistics, keyword analysis, and descriptive network visualization. RESULTS: A total of 9671 publications were identified. Research output increased markedly over the study period, with publications from 2020 onward accounting for 84.9% of the literature. Original research articles published in English predominated. The Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling, Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences, and Briefings in Bioinformatics were the leading publication venues. China, India, and South Korea were the most productive countries based on corresponding author affiliation. Drug Design and Modeling was the predominant thematic domain, encompassing 42.1% of publications, whereas Clinical Pharmacology and Precision Therapeutics represented 3.6%. Pharmacy Operations and Clinical Decision Support (1.6%), Pharmacovigilance and Medication Safety (1.2%), Clinical Trials and Drug Development (0.6%), and Pharmaceutical Manufacturing and Supply Chain Management (0.5%) were comparatively underrepresented. Citation analysis indicated that the most influential publications were primarily methodological AI studies rather than pharmacy-specific applications. CONCLUSIONS: AI-related research in PPS has expanded rapidly but remains predominantly focused on computational drug discovery and preclinical applications. Greater emphasis on clinical implementation, patient-centered pharmacy practice, pharmacovigilance, and broader geographic participation is needed to support equitable translation of AI into pharmaceutical care.

titulo: Assessment of Medication Regimen Complexity and Adherence in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Patients at a Tertiary Care Teaching Hospital.
autores_exibicao: Bhandari K, Marasine NR, Bist CD, Pant P
resumo: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Medication regimen complexity and poor adherence are major barriers to optimal management, yet limited evidence exists in Nepal. This study aimed to assess medication regimen complexity and adherence among COPD patients attending a tertiary care hospital in Nepal. METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from November 2023 to May 2024 at a tertiary care teaching hospital in Nepal. A total of 174 COPD patients aged ≥40 years were enrolled using convenience sampling. Medication regimen complexity was assessed using the validated 65-item Medication Regimen Complexity Index (MRCI), and adherence was evaluated with the Nepali version of the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-8). Pearson's chi-square test and binary logistic regression were performed at a 5% level of significance to examine factors associated with medication nonadherence. RESULTS: Of the total, 46.6% demonstrated suboptimal adherence, strongly associated with smoking (adjusted odds ratios [aOR]: 7.5; 95% CI: 2.82-19.90; p < 0.001) and alcohol use (aOR: 3.66; 95% CI: 1.578-8.49; p = 0.003). COPD regimens exhibited higher complexity (mean MRCI: 10.296 ± 5.4) than non-COPD medications (3.66 ± 3.478). High COPD MRCI (aOR: 25.8; 95% CI: 14.7-38.5; p = 0.03) and high patient-level MRCI (aOR: 15.6; 95% CI: 6.7-33.9; p < 0.001) were significant predictors of nonadherence. CONCLUSION: COPD-specific regimens were found to be more complex, and higher regimen complexity together with lifestyle factors, such as smoking and alcohol consumption, were strong determinants of nonadherence. Simplifying regimens through fixed-dose combinations, pharmacist-led interventions, and behavioral counseling may improve medication adherence and treatment outcomes in COPD patients.

titulo: Bedside pharmacist interventions for managing intravenous drug incompatibilities in critically ill patients.
autores_exibicao: de Souza AC, Neves JDR, da Silva Terres ALF, da Silva GG, de Almeida LF, Couto A, Elias SC, de Castilho SR
periodico: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
resumo: BACKGROUND: Patients admitted to intensive care units are at increased risk of intravenous drug incompatibilities, owing to polypharmacy and the limited number of available venous access devices. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate bedside pharmacist interventions for managing drug incompatibilities identified during intravenous administration in intensive care unit patients. METHODS: A cross-sectional study with prospective data collection was conducted between June and December 2025 in five intensive care units of a university hospital. Two pharmacists assessed medication administration at the bedside and checked compatibility using the Micromedex and American Society of Health-System Pharmacists (ASHP) Injectable Drug Information databases. The type and number of central venous access devices, infusion modality, proposed interventions, and the healthcare team's response were recorded. Data were described using absolute and relative frequencies. RESULTS: A total of 887 infusions were analyzed in 88 patients, of which 159 corresponded to occurrences of incompatibility or lack of compatibility data (73 distinct drug combinations). Of these 159 occurrences, 135 (84.9%) were incompatible, and 24 (15.1%) lacked compatibility studies. Most of the pharmacist interventions performed were accepted by the healthcare team (130/159; 81.8%). CONCLUSIONS: The high frequency of incompatibilities observed is related to the large number of intravenous medications and the complexity of therapeutic regimens used in intensive care. Bedside pharmacist involvement proved feasible and contributed to safer medication administration practices in these units.

titulo: Community pharmacists' views on the factors influencing prescription medication side effect counselling: a qualitative interview study.
autores_exibicao: Evrard P, Crowley M, Otway T, Dalton K
resumo: INTRODUCTION: Community pharmacists play a crucial role in medication counselling, which includes side effect counselling (SEC), helping support informed decision-making, patients' adherence, and medication safety. Despite its recognised importance, deficiencies in SEC provision have been reported, and limited research has investigated the behavioural determinants underpinning pharmacists' SEC practices. AIM: This qualitative study aimed to explore community pharmacists' views on the factors influencing prescription medication SEC. METHOD: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with community pharmacists in Ireland. Transcripts were analysed using conventional content analysis and directed content analysis by using the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF). Predominant domains were determined based on the frequency of the beliefs, presence of conflicting beliefs, and perceived strengths of those beliefs. RESULTS: From eleven interviews, six predominant TDF domains were identified in influencing SEC provision: environmental context and resources, social professional role and identity, memory, attention and decision-making, skills, beliefs about consequences, and social influences. While SEC was considered a core professional responsibility, time pressures and workload were dominant environmental barriers. Pharmacists employ cognitive heuristics to prioritise SEC for new and high-risk medications and tailor their language and information quantity based on patients' health literacy and emotional state to balance the need to inform against the risk of hindering adherence by overwhelming patients-skills which they believed they refined with experience. CONCLUSION: This study provides unique insights into the behavioural determinants influencing pharmacist SEC. The findings offer a foundation for developing targeted interventions to enhance SEC in community pharmacy, ultimately helping to improve patient safety and therapeutic outcomes.

titulo: Enhancing adverse drug reaction reporting through a pharmacy-led multi-component intervention: A real-world pre-post evaluation.
autores_exibicao: Alruwaili M, Abu-Huwaij R, Khaleel MA
periodico: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
resumo: BACKGROUND: Underreporting of adverse drug reactions (ADRs) remains a major challenge in pharmacovigilance despite established reporting systems in Saudi Arabia. Limited healthcare professional (HCP) engagement, inadequate awareness, and low patient participation contribute to low reporting rates, while evidence on integrated real-world interventions remains scarce. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and real-world impact of a pragmatic, multi-component intervention combining HCP education, community engagement, and a QR code-based digital ADR reporting system. METHODS: A quasi-experimental pre-post study was conducted at Turaif General Hospital, Saudi Arabia. Seventy-eight matched HCPs completed validated questionnaires before and after the intervention to assess ADR reporting knowledge, perceptions, barriers, and facilitators. The intervention included implementation of a QR code-based reporting system in the outpatient pharmacy, targeted HCP education, and community awareness activities. ADR reports during a 4-month baseline period were compared with those from a 4-month post-intervention period. RESULTS: HCP knowledge (mean difference = 0.311; p = 0.0092) and perceptions (mean difference = 0.354; p = 0.0037) improved significantly after the intervention, whereas perceived barriers and facilitators did not change significantly. ADR reports increased from 11 at baseline to 156 post-intervention, representing a 14.2-fold increase. Patients and the public submitted 33% of all reports. CONCLUSION: This pragmatic, pharmacy-led intervention was feasible and substantially improved HCP knowledge, perceptions, and ADR reporting. Integrating digital reporting with professional education and community engagement may strengthen patient-centered pharmacovigilance and medication safety.

titulo: Functional health literacy and medication adherence in atrial fibrillation patients.
autores_exibicao: Janjani P, Haraj A, Nosrati P, Hasani V, Ardalan P, Hasani S, Moradinia S, Khodaie MM et al. (12 autores)
periodico: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
resumo: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) treatment requires strict, long-term adherence to oral anticoagulants (OACs) to decrease associated morbidity risks. Despite its importance, adherence varies widely; nonadherence contributes to life-threatening adverse outcomes and elevated costs. Health literacy (HL)-the ability to acquire, comprehend, evaluate, and apply health information-is an important, yet underestimated factor. Given conflicting evidence on the HL-adherence association in chronic diseases, this study investigated this relationship and influencing demographic/contextual factors in AF patients across Iran. METHODS: This descriptive-analytical cross-sectional, multicenter study was conducted in 2025 across Tehran, Kurdistan, and Kermanshah provinces on 407 adult AF patients receiving OAC therapy. Functional HL was assessed using the HELIA questionnaire; medication adherence was evaluated via MMAS-8. Analysis involved Pearson correlation, independent-samples t-tests, and multiple linear regression. RESULTS: Mean total HL score was 108.65 ± 30.96 (moderate); mean MMAS-8 was 2.61 ± 1.54 (relatively high adherence). Total HL demonstrated a significant negative correlation with MMAS-8 scores (r = -0.099, p < 0.05), indicating higher HL associates with improved adherence, driven primarily by the "Information" subscale (r = -0.172, p < 0.01). While males had significantly higher HL scores (p < 0.001), females showed better adherence (p = 0.045). Notably, older age was paradoxically linked to worse adherence in Kurdistan (r = 0.327, p < 0.01). In multiple linear regression adjusting for age, gender, and study site (R2 = 0.214, p < 0.001), total HL emerged as a strong independent predictor of better adherence (β = -0.500, p < 0.001), alongside older age, female gender, and residing in Kurdistan (all p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Health literacy is a statistically significant, independent and modifiable predictor of medication adherence in Iranian AF populations. Efficacy is specific to functional information application, highlighting the need for interventions focused on practical skills. The complex age-gender interaction demonstrates how regional socioeconomic and cultural contexts affect the HL-adherence relationship.

autores_exibicao: Kiratli Nalbant E, Ismail Mendi B
resumo: BACKGROUND: Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKis) are increasingly used in dermatology, yet their gastrointestinal safety profiles remain incompletely characterized in real-world practice. Although gastrointestinal adverse events (GIAEs) are generally mild, gastrointestinal perforation remains an important safety concern with JAKi treatment. This study aimed to characterize GIAEs associated with six oral JAKis and identify potential disproportionality signals in the US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). METHODS: GIAEs associated with abrocitinib, baricitinib, deucravacitinib, ritlecitinib, tofacitinib, and upadacitinib were evaluated. titulo: Health literacy, medication adherence, and quality-of-life scores in Jordanian adults with chronic diseases: a dual analytical study using the long-term conditions questionnaire and the EuroQol five-dimension three-level questionnaire.
autores_exibicao: Al-Qerem W, Jarab A, Eberhardt J, Abdo S, Al-Saa'di L, Al-Shehadeh R, Khasim D, Zumot R et al. (9 autores)
resumo: AIMS: This study examined the association of health literacy with quality-of-life outcomes among Jordanian adults with chronic diseases using two patient-reported outcome measures, the Long-Term Conditions Questionnaire (LTCQ) and the EuroQol five-dimension, three-level questionnaire (EQ-5D-3L). It also compared conventional regression and machine-learning (ML) approaches for modelling these relationships. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional online study, Arabic-language questionnaires were completed by Jordanian adults aged 18 years or older with at least one chronic physical, mental, or neurological condition. The survey, designed to take 10-12 minutes, included the LTCQ, EQ-5D-3L, Medication Adherence Report Scale (MARS-5), and 12-item Health Literacy Scale (HLS-Q12). A total of 901 complete responses were analyzed. Data were split into training (n = 633) and test (n = 268) sets. Multiple linear regression was used for LTCQ, Tobit regression for EQ-5D-3L index scores, and ML models were trained to explore nonlinear associations. RESULTS: Health literacy and medication adherence were positively associated with both LTCQ (beta = 3.923 and 2.219, respectively; both p < 0.001) and EQ-5D-3L index scores (beta = 0.025, p = 0.001; beta = 0.020, p = 0.009). Number of medications was inversely associated with both outcomes. LTCQ was more strongly linked with psychosocial and self-management variables, whereas EQ-5D-3L was more closely aligned with medication burden and clinical comorbidity. These findings should be interpreted as associative rather than causal and as differences in captured dimensions rather than evidence of instrument superiority.

titulo: 'Life has become a lot easier'-the acceptability of the treatable traits clinic experience to people with bronchiectasis.
autores_exibicao: Krieg KE, Lee AL, Dale MJ, Dwyer TJ, McKeough ZJ
resumo: INTRODUCTION: The treatable traits approach involves the identification of traits that are measurable and clinically relevant to the patient, which informs an individualized management plan. While improved quality of life and health outcomes have been demonstrated, the acceptability of this approach to people with bronchiectasis has not been explored. The aim of our study was to explore the acceptability of the treatable traits approach to people with bronchiectasis in a regional setting. PATIENTS AND METHODS: An exploratory qualitative study. Interviews were conducted with adults who first attended an outpatient bronchiectasis clinic in regional Australia, which had implemented the treatable traits approach. The interview guide was developed to explore the seven components of the theoretical framework of acceptability. Engagement with the transcripts occurred using the six phases of thematic analysis to develop key themes. RESULTS: Ten participants were included (age 37-82 years; female sex, 70%; Bronchiectasis Severity Index, mild, 20%; moderate, 50%; and severe, 30%). This study reports three themes. 'A tool kit to support my health' explores the contribution of individualized and multifaceted interventions to a perceived improvement in respiratory health. 'Better health, better self' captures the patient-reported impact of improved respiratory health on quality of life. 'Some things don't change' describes the ongoing challenges for people living with bronchiectasis that are not impacted by the clinic interventions. CONCLUSION: People with bronchiectasis from a single regional Australian clinic described a highly valued and acceptable clinic experience, with perceived improvements in respiratory health and overall well-being despite significant ongoing impacts on daily life. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered in the Australian and New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (https://www.anzctr.org.au/, ACTRN12620000377932).

titulo: Association Between Early Joint Awareness and Falls After Total Hip Arthroplasty.
autores_exibicao: Wada O, Nagai K, Igeta M, Mori A, Mizuno K
resumo: BACKGROUND: The Forgotten Joint Score-12 (FJS-12) is a patient-reported outcome measure of joint awareness after total hip arthroplasty (THA). Falls after THA remain clinically important. However, longitudinal evidence regarding the associations among early FJS-12, subsequent falls, and later recovery of joint unawareness remains limited. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used a prospectively maintained institutional database from a single Japanese institution. Consecutive patients who underwent primary THA between January 2021 and December 2023 were included. FJS-12 was assessed at 3 and 12 months postoperatively, and falls occurring between 3 and 12 months postoperatively were identified at the 12-month visit based on patients' self-report over this 9-month interval. Modified Poisson regression was used to examine the association between FJS at 3 months and subsequent falls. Multiple linear regression was used to examine the association between fall occurrence and FJS at 12 months, adjusting for FJS at 3 months. RESULTS: Overall, 623 patients were analyzed (mean age 70.8 years; 85.2% female). Ninety-nine patients (15.9%) experienced at least 1 fall between 3 and 12 months postoperatively. Lower FJS at 3 months was associated with a higher risk of subsequent falls. Fall occurrence was associated with lower FJS at 12 months, independent of FJS at 3 months and other covariates. CONCLUSIONS: Early postoperative joint awareness was associated with subsequent falls after THA, and falls were associated with lower FJS at 12 months. The FJS-12 may provide additional patient-reported information when assessing postoperative fall risk.

titulo: Associations of seated dual-task ergometer training with cognitive and mobility outcomes in older adults with disabling conditions undergoing inpatient convalescent rehabilitation: a retrospective observational study.
autores_exibicao: Hasui M, Takashima S, Suzuki M, Isobe T, Yamashita Y, Kurotobi Y, Yamauchi K
resumo: OBJECTIVE: To examine associations between a 4-week seated dual-task (DT) ergometer program and cognitive and mobility outcomes in older convalescent rehabilitation inpatients. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 125 rehabilitation episodes involving older adults undergoing inpatient convalescent rehabilitation , primarily for orthopaedic disorders and stroke. Participants received seated DT ergometer training (n = 79) or conventional recumbent ergometer exercise (n = 46) for 4 weeks. Primary outcomes were the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Trail Making Test-Japanese Part A (TMT-J Part A), 10-m DT walking time, and the Timed Up and Go test (TUG). Analysis of covariance models adjusted post-training outcomes for baseline values, age, and diagnosis using HC3 robust standard errors. RESULTS: Adjusted between-group differences (DT minus conventional exercise) were nonsignificant for MMSE (0.08 points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.78 to 0.93; p = 0.862), TMT-J Part A (-6.59 s; 95% CI, -22.06 to 8.87; p = 0.403), DT walking time (-0.89 s; 95% CI, -2.77 to 0.99; p = 0.354), and TUG (-0.97 s; 95% CI, -2.62 to 0.67; p = 0.246). The six-sessions-per-week sensitivity analysis yielded consistent results. Exploratory analyses showed greater improvements in DT walking time (p = 0.003) and TUG (p = 0.016) in the MMSE ≥27 stratum. Within standard TMT-J limits, adjusted Part A time was shorter in the DT group (p = 0.035), whereas the unadjusted change-score comparison was nonsignificant (p = 0.182). CONCLUSIONS: Seated DT ergometer training did not demonstrate a clear advantage over conventional ergometer exercise in cognitive or mobility outcomes. Exploratory findings are hypothesis-generating. Prospective randomized studies with standardized training exposure are needed.

titulo: Comparative effects of motor-control interventions on neuromuscular and biomechanical outcomes after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
autores_exibicao: Liang F, Ma L, Liang J, Xiong Z
tipo: Journal Article, Systematic Review, Network Meta-Analysis, Review
resumo: BACKGROUND: Neuromuscular-control and biomechanical deficits may persist after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR). Comparative motor-control effects remain uncertain. OBJECTIVES: To compare motor-control interventions after ACLR. DESIGN: Systematic review and network meta-analysis. METHOD: Seven databases were searched to 12 May 2026. Usual rehabilitation comprised conventional symptom control, motion, strengthening, gait, or functional training. Three neuromuscular-control outcomes underwent network meta-analysis; k ≥ 2 biomechanical comparisons were pooled and k = 1 estimates unpooled. RoB 2 assessed bias; CINeMA and GRADE assessed confidence. RESULTS: Thirty-two trials enrolled 1437 participants. Proprioceptive training improved joint position sense versus usual rehabilitation (SMD 1.02, 95% CI 0.54-1.50; moderate CINeMA confidence); jump-landing control training yielded a favorable dynamic-balance estimate versus usual rehabilitation (1.19, 0.59-1.80; low CINeMA confidence) and was sensitive to exclusion of a late-phase multi-arm athlete trial; feedback-enhanced (0.88, 0.43-1.32) and proprioceptive training (0.59, 0.21-0.97) favored postural control (both low CINeMA confidence). Pooled estimates suggested that neuromuscular training may improve knee valgus and knee flexion kinematics during single-leg landing (1.51, 0.51-2.51; 1.07, 0.49-1.65); pooled gait biomechanical symmetry was inconclusive (-0.41, -0.87-0.05). Across networks, τ² ranged from 0.0275 to 0.1698; global tests detected no statistically clear inconsistency (P = 0.087-0.229), although sparse loop structures limited inference. CONCLUSION: Moderate-confidence evidence supported proprioceptive training for improving joint position sense after ACLR. Other interventions may help balance and landing control, but their benefits are less certain. The evidence does not establish a single best approach across outcomes.

titulo: Economic evaluation of long-term manual therapy for chronic neck pain: A Markov model-based analysis.
autores_exibicao: Kim DY, Kim E, Lim YC, Kim EY, Lee YS, Ha IH, Lee YJ
resumo: BACKGROUND: The global burden of chronic neck pain is rising, increasing the importance of cost-effective pain management. Manual therapy may reduce economic and societal burden by preventing chronic pain recurrence, but supporting evidence is limited. This study evaluates the long-term cost-effectiveness of manual therapy compared with standard care for chronic neck pain. METHODS: A Markov model with three-month cycles is used to simulate health-state transitions over three years. Treatment alternatives include Chuna manual therapy (10 sessions twice weekly for five weeks) and usual care (oral medication and physical therapy, administered with the same frequency as Chuna). Clinical and economic data were sourced from pragmatic randomized controlled trials and official public documents. Costs (medical and non-medical) and utilities were estimated from the healthcare system and societal perspectives, and utility weights derived from the EuroQol five-dimension five-level scale. Sensitivity analyses assessed parameter uncertainty, including one-way and probabilistic sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Over three years, Chuna manual therapy involved an additional cost of only $407, yielding 0.03 more quality-adjusted life years (QALY) compared to usual care, resulting in an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of $14,125/QALY. Sensitivity analyses confirm cost-effectiveness at a willingness-to-pay threshold of $26,375/QALY in most scenarios. Probabilistic sensitivity analyses reveal cost-effectiveness probabilities of 77.2% and 98.5% from the healthcare and societal perspective, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Chuna manual therapy is a cost-effective intervention with clinical and economic advantages over usual care. The findings support policy decisions on extending health insurance coverage for long-term manual therapy and provide a foundation for future studies.

titulo: Efficacy of Sensory Electrical Stimulation Versus Alternating Electromyography-Guided Electrical Stimulation on Functional Recovery of the Hand in Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
autores_exibicao: Habib DAA, Emam M, Elsayed A, El-Sherbini AEIEM, Ahmed RAMA
tipo: Journal Article, Randomized Controlled Trial, Comparative Study
resumo: BackgroundImpaired hand function can limit independence. Sensory electrical stimulation (SES) and alternating electromyography-guided electrical stimulation (Alt-EMG) differ in stimulation characteristics and voluntary effort requirements, but comparative evidence is limited.ObjectiveTo compare SES and Alt-EMG, each combined with conventional physical therapy, on upper-limb motor function, spasticity, and muscle strength in chronic stroke.MethodsThis three-arm, assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial included 60 adults aged 45-65 years, 6-18 months post-stroke, allocated equally to SES, Alt-EMG, or control groups (n = 20 each). The primary outcome was the Action Research Arm Test (ARAT); Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) and Medical Research Council (MRC) scores were secondary outcomes. ARAT was analyzed using ANCOVA adjusted for baseline score and age; ordinal outcomes were analyzed nonparametrically. Benjamini-Hochberg and Holm corrections addressed multiplicity.ResultsAll participants completed the 12-week intervention. Treatment group significantly predicted adjusted post-intervention ARAT scores (F (2,55) = 23.19, P < .001, partial η2=.46). Adjusted mean gains versus control were 12.05 points for SES and 12.44 points for Alt-EMG (both P < .001), with no significant difference between active groups. Significant between-group differences were observed for shoulder, elbow, and wrist spasticity and most muscle-strength measures, except finger extensors.ConclusionsSES and Alt-EMG combined with conventional physical therapy produced greater improvement in upper-limb motor function than conventional physical therapy alone over 12 weeks. No difference was observed between SES and Alt-EMG for the primary outcome.

titulo: Efficacy of adding fascial manipulation to neuromuscular electrical stimulation and sling exercise for postpartum diastasis recti: A randomized controlled trial.
autores_exibicao: Chen C, Qu Q, Xu H, Xiao Y, Li L, Tian Y, Wang Q, Zhang H et al. (9 autores)
resumo: PURPOSE: This trial assessed whether adding fascial manipulation to neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) plus sling exercise, with increased treatment time and therapist contact, improves outcomes in postpartum diastasis recti. METHODS: In this outcome-assessor-blinded, two-arm randomized controlled trial, 96 postpartum women with diastasis recti abdominis were randomised (permuted blocks of four) to fascial manipulation plus NMES and sling exercise (60 min/session) or standard NMES plus sling exercise (40 min/session), three times weekly for 6 weeks. No adverse reactions were observed. RESULTS: Within both groups, IRD, pelvic anterior tilt and VAS decreased and standing time and SF-36 increased (all p < 0.001). Between-group change scores favoured the intervention for pain (ΔVAS -2.51 [-3.50, -0.39] vs -0.52 [-0.97, 0.00], p < 0.001, r = -0.51) and pelvic tilt (-2.84 [-4.72, -0.74] vs -1.10 [-3.02, 0.00], p = 0.008, r = -0.31), remaining significant after false-discovery-rate correction (q < 0.05). ΔIRD (p = 0.042) and ΔGlazer (p = 0.036) were nominally significant but did not survive correction (q = 0.073). Differences in standing time, SF-36 and body fat were not significant. Exploratory responder analysis: 52.1% vs 8.3% achieved a ≥ 2-point VAS reduction (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Adding fascial manipulation to NMES plus sling exercise yields robust benefits for pain relief and pelvic tilt correction, with nominal effects on IRD and pelvic floor function; the proposed fascial mechanism remains unconfirmed. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Postpartum diastasis recti impairs core stability and quality of life, yet rehabilitation often neglects abdominal fascial dysfunction. In this assessor-blinded randomised trial, adding fascial manipulation to neuromuscular electrical stimulation plus sling exercise produced robust between-group benefits for pain relief (large effect; 52.1% vs 8.3% achieving a clinically meaningful reduction) and pelvic tilt correction (medium effect), with smaller, nominal effects on inter-rectus distance and pelvic floor function; balance and quality-of-life differences were not significant. Tissue-level mechanisms of fascial release remain unconfirmed.

titulo: Factors associated with Severe Balance Impairment After Right-Hemisphere Stroke: The Role of Spatial Neglect and Lateropulsion: A Secondary Analysis of Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study POSTIM.
autores_exibicao: Foussat E, Painchaud S, Leplaideur S, Rousseau C, Viallard L, Bonan I, Jamal K
tipo: Journal Article, Multicenter Study, Randomized Controlled Trial
resumo: BackgroundBalance impairment remains a major concern after right-hemisphere stroke (RHS), even after regaining unsupported standing, reflecting multifactorial and insufficiently explored postural control deficits.ObjectiveTo identify factors associated with balance impairment and to assess its severity using the Berg Balance Scale (BBS), in RHS patients who have recovered unsupported standing but exhibit marked weight-bearing asymmetry.MethodsThis cross-sectional secondary analysis used baseline data (May 2013-May 2018) from a multicenter randomized controlled trial on weight-bearing asymmetry, across eight French rehabilitation centers. Patients aged 18-80 with a first right supratentorial stroke within 9 months, standing unassisted for 30 s with eyes closed, and bearing <40% body weight on the paretic leg were included. BBS scores <45/56 defined severe balance impairment associated with increased fall risk. Lower-limb motor deficits, spasticity, sensory function, lateropulsion, spatial neglect, and body perception were analyzed using univariate and multivariable logistic regression.ResultsAmong 82 patients (mean age 59.3 ± 10.3 years; post-stroke delay 91.3 ± 59.6 days), 61(74%) had a BBS <45/56. titulo: High- and moderate-intensity interval training for cardiac-psychological comorbidity: Results from a 4-week intervention.
autores_exibicao: Song Q, Bai B, Chang J, Jiang Z, Lin Z, Hu D, Ma H
resumo: BACKGROUND: Anxiety and depressive symptoms are common in patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and are associated with poorer prognosis. Exercise-based rehabilitation may improve both psychological and cardiopulmonary outcomes in this population. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the short-term effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and moderate-intensity interval training (MIIT) in CVD patients with comorbid anxiety and/or depression. METHODS: This retrospective real-world study screened 1020 cardiac rehabilitation patients, of whom 112 were included in the final analysis. All participants completed a 4-week supervised outpatient HIIT or MIIT. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed using the GAD-7 and PHQ-9, and cardiopulmonary fitness was evaluated by standardized cardiopulmonary exercise testing. RESULTS: After 4 weeks, in the HIIT group, GAD-7 and PHQ-9 scores decreased by 4.4 ± 4.3 and 3.7 ± 4.3 points (Cohen's d = -1.023 and -0.860; p < 0.001); in the MIIT group, the corresponding reductions were 4.8 ± 4.9 and 3.5 ± 4.0 points (Cohen's d = -0.980 and -0.875; p < 0.001). Both groups also demonstrated significant improvements in multiple cardiopulmonary parameters (all p < 0.05). Nominal between-group differences were observed for AT VO₂ and PETCO₂ before multiplicity correction, but neither difference remained statistically significant after FDR correction. CONCLUSIONS: In clinical practice, short-term HIIT and MIIT may both be feasible strategies to alleviate psychological symptoms and improve cardiopulmonary fitness in CVD patients with comorbid anxiety or depression.
